data.cultural_impact: The term "Gita" is most famously known as the sacred Sanskrit text, Bhagavad Gita, which is a part of the Mahabharata epic. This philosophical and spiritual classic permeates every aspect of Indian culture, from scriptures, mythology, arts, and daily life. It is widely regarded as a fundamental scientific, ethical, and spiritual guide for many Hindus. The Bhagavad Gita is also popularly referred to as 'the song of God' or 'God’s song to the heart of Arjuna.'
data.spiritual_significance: The Bhagavad Gita is considered a profound and timeless spiritual text that offers guidance on the attainment of self-realization and union with the divine. It narrates a conversation between Lord Krishna and Arjuna, delving into a myriad of topics about life, dharma, karma, love, and its ultimate meaning. The text is a compilation of timeless wisdom and universal truths, framing a spiritual path that transcends the boundaries of nationality and culture. The Bhagavad Gita's profound exploration of diverse aspects of human existence and its practical advice on leading an ethical and purposeful life makes it a valuable companion to the seeker of inner peace and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name "Gita" in Hinduism symbolizes the essence of the Bhagavad Gita, a sacred text that imparts the wisdom of Bhagavan (God) to Arjuna. It represents the inner guide (the 'Gita' in one's heart) that illuminates the path to spiritual growth and self-realization.

vedic_reference.note: Refers to the Bhagavad Gita, a sacred Hindu scripture, where the god Krishna imparts spiritual knowledge to Arjuna.

historical_references.reference: The Bhagavad Gita is a 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the Indian epic Mahabharata. It is set in the Indian subcontinent during the 2nd century BCE and is a conversation between Prince Arjuna and the god Krishna.

The Bhagavad Gita is considered one of the most important texts in the Hindu religion. It was compiled between the 4th and 6th centuries CE, although its origins are believed to be much older. The text is a conversation between Prince Arjuna and the god Krishna, who serves as his charioteer and spiritual guide, and is set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra during the great war between the Pandava and Kuru armies.
historical_references.context: Battlefield of Kurukshetra, Pandava and Kuru armies

modern_usage.modern_context: The Sanskrit word 'Gita' is derived from the ancient Hindu text 'Bhagavad Gita'. In modern times, this revered name has been adopted in various contexts, reflecting its timeless wisdom and relevance. In the tech industry, numerous tech companies have named themselves after this ancient text, symbolizing the quest for knowledge and understanding. On mobile apps platforms, the 'Gita Quotes' app has gained immense popularity, offering users easy access to inspiring quotes and verses from the Bhagavad Gita. Lastly, social media has become a hub for various Gita study groups where individuals can discuss, learn, and share their insights on this profound text.
